# Tfa066 — Pipe-like face with seam edge wrongly removed as "small"

<!-- Auto-generated; edit `STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.md` instead. -->

**Section**: §12.3c (`12-3c-faces`)  
**Fixture**: [`step-examples/12-3c-faces/Tfa066.stp`](../../step-examples/12-3c-faces/Tfa066.stp)  

## Sources
- OCCT MANTIS#0022586

## Description

A long thin pipe face (length ≫ width, e.g., 100 × 0.1 mm) has a seam edge from the closed surface. A "small face" detector classifies it as small because its bounding-box width is below threshold and removes it — losing a structurally significant part of the shell.

## Reproducer recipe

Cylindrical face length 100 mm, radius 0.05 mm (so bbox width is 0.1 mm). A small-face detector with width threshold 0.5 mm flags it for removal.

## Expected kernel behavior

small-face detection must use area, not bounding-box minor dimension; long thin features are not "small".
